messages:
ashley: Heads up — we're seeing a ~3x spike in GPU pod preemptions in ap-southeast1. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd123/evictions?orgId=1 :eyes: Cost blip and a bunch of user jobs are failing. Might be related to the taint/label rollout earlier this morning.
mike: yikes :eyes: can you drop the link?
ashley: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd123/evictions?panelId=7 — spike at 04:12 UTC. Also noticed many pods landing on nodes with taint `compute:new` even though a chunk of pods don't have the matching toleration.
jia: we merged the taint-add PR with the intention that workloads would be updated by helm charts. maybe some jobs missed the change. could be toleration mismatch.
ashley: yeah, looking at pod specs some inference jobs have toleration `compute:new:v1` but older jobs used `compute:new` (no version). scheduler seems to be treating the unversioned toleration as matching, which lets small standalone jobs land on dedicated-gpu nodes -> fragmentation and subsequent gang evictions.
nate: i'll grep admission logs + node binds real quick. give me a minute.
nate: ```kubectl get pods -n prod -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,TOL:.spec.tolerations | grep inference | head```
(nate output) `inference-a-xyz   gpu-node-32   [compute:new]` — yep, several live pods missing the versioned toleration.
mike: also seeing a ton of tiny sidecar-only pods with nodeAffinity nvlink==present landing on same rack as large gangs. packing small stuff onto big racks causes gang scheduling to fail and triggers preemptive eviction thrash.
jia: action: recommend pausing taint rollout. i'll open rollback. we can also add a validation webhook to enforce `compute:new:v1` toleration on helm chart templates.
ashley: agree. rolling rollback across the ap-southeast pool now, starting with two AZs.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job started for `taint-rollout-pr-432` on pool ap-southeast1-a -> ap-southeast1-c
nate: after rollback evictions dropped back to baseline within ~2m, cost anomaly diminishing. good sign. we should still follow up with a short postmortem.
jia: i'll create an issue (infra#789) to: 1) add admission-level check for toleration format, 2) update helm charts for legacy jobs, 3) add an autoscaler annotation to avoid packing tiny pods onto dedicated racks, and 4) add an e2e test that simulates mixed-version tolerations.
mike: also propose new alert: `gpu_pod_eviction_rate{region="ap-southeast1"} > 0.5` for 5m to P0 oncall. catch earlier.
ashley: thanks all — I'll update the incident doc and ping support to notify impacted customers.
